I rewrote the skill's description in `skills/parquet-schema-check/SKILL.md:3`. I haven't tested it yet, so I don't know whether agents will now load it.

**The cause:** the description was `Helps with parquet files.` The description is the only part of a skill that agents see when deciding whether to load it. "Helps with" gives no situation to match, so nothing about writing a parquet file pointed to this skill.

**The new description:**
> Use when about to write or overwrite a parquet file (to_parquet, pyarrow write_table, write.parquet) for a dataset with a schema in schemas/, or when a job reading a parquet file fails on a missing column, column order or dtype mismatch.

- It names the moment to load the skill (about to write a parquet file) and the calls an agent would actually be typing.
- It also triggers on the failure the skill exists to prevent: a downstream job breaking on columns or dtypes.
- It doesn't summarise the skill's steps. If it did, agents might follow the summary and skip the body, including the "don't cast to make them match" rule.
- The main trigger comes first, so it survives if a runtime shortens long descriptions in its skill list.
- I didn't change the body.

**Still to do:**
- **Re-run your baseline scenarios with this description.** That's the only way to know if it fixed the problem. Your baseline results aren't saved anywhere in the repo, so I can't re-run them from here. If you point me to the scenarios or paste them, I'll write them to `specs/baseline/` (outside the skill folder, so they don't ship with it) and compare.
- **The call names are a guess.** I picked them from the body's "frame" and "dtypes", which suggests pandas or pyarrow. If you write parquet with something else (polars `write_parquet`, Spark, DuckDB `COPY`), tell me and I'll change them.
- **There's no `license` field.** The skill-writing guide asks for one, but nothing in this repo requires it and no other skill has one, so I left it out. Tell me if you want one added.
- **Nothing is committed yet.**
